Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

metacleaner 2.0.0

First release as an R package. This is a complete rewrite of the Python/R command-line scripts (metacleaner.py + taxafilter.R) released as v1.0.0 on GitHub.

New features

  • One function, clean_reference(), runs the whole workflow; write_results() saves the cleaned FASTA, taxonomy, a report of flagged sequences and a summary.
  • Built-in C++ search engine: BLAST+, Python, pyfasta and shell tools are no longer required. Multithreaded on all platforms (threads, or threads = "auto"). BLAST+ can still be used with engine = "blast".
  • Taxonomy can come from a taxonomy file (taxonomizr/MetaCurator CSV, QIIME-style lineage strings or a table), from NCBI web services (taxonomy = "ncbi", only the needed accessions are looked up), from a local taxonomizr database, or from several of these in turn.
  • build_reference_db() and download_ncbi_sequences() replace the shell recipe for building reference and contaminant databases; read_fasta(), write_fasta(), dereplicate() and extract_accession() replace the awk/perl/sed/seqkit steps.
  • FASTA files may be wrapped or gzip-compressed.

Bug fixes relative to the command-line version

  • Queries with no BLAST hit at all in the reference database were never flagged; they were written to the clean FASTA but were missing from the clean taxonomy file. They are now flagged as “no match in reference database”.
  • BLAST output was processed in blocks of 10,000 lines, so a query whose hits were split across two blocks could be judged on only part of its hits.
  • The automatic taxonomizr database build could never run.
  • The taxonomy step crashed when no sequence was flagged.
  • A dot in a directory name broke the search step.
  • Flag reasons always said “genera”, whatever --filterlevel was used.
  • Database names were used as regular expressions to split the flagged list, so similar database names (e.g. ITS and ITS_plant) were confused.
  • The superkingdom rank no longer exists in current taxonomizr databases (it is now domain); this is handled transparently.
  • pyfasta, required for chunking, does not run under Python 3.

Changes in behavior

  • The flagged-sequence report has one row per sequence (previously one row per hit) and new columns database, identity, coverage, n_hits and hit_taxa.
  • Up to max_hits = 100 qualifying hits per query are used in the taxonomy checks (previously BLAST’s -max_target_seqs 10).
